speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I notice you have provided no specific details about your skin condition yet. To begin our evaluation, can you describe the appearance, size, and duration of the lesion you are most concerned about?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC).

The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusty lesions on the penile shaft and a finger, combined with a significant smoking history and failed treatments for syphilis or eczema, strongly suggests SCC. I am requesting a biopsy of the penile lesion and a full-body skin examination to confirm the diagnosis and rule out metastasis or other malignancies.
